name: Memory Consolidation
description: Transfer of memories from hippocampal storage (episodic) to cortical storage (semantic, long-term). Occurs via replay during sleep. Integrates new learning with existing knowledge. Distinct from working memory maintenance: operates on longer timescales (hours to days).
key_references: McClelland, J. L., McNaughton, B. L., & O'Reilly, R. C. (1995). Why there are complementary learning systems in the hippocampus and neocortex: Insights from the successes and failures of connectionist models of learning and memory. Psychological Review, 102(3), 419-457.
Born, J., Rasch, B., & Gais, S. (2006). Sleep to remember. The Neuroscientist, 12(5), 410-424.
empirical_evidence: Sleep deprivation impairs long-term memory. Hippocampal-cortical dialog during sleep via replay. fMRI shows memory replay during sleep. Gradual emergence of cortical dependency for memories (systems consolidation). Complementary learning systems theory well-supported. Molecular mechanisms involving protein synthesis documented.
